description: We are Cosmic Coders 26, a team of passionate students interested in space, web development and hackathons. Our goal is to learn, collaborate and build a working browser game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, where kids (7-12) run a Mars outpost using real NASA space weather data. We are looking for teammates in web dev, game design, graphic design or kid-friendly writing. Beginners welcome, join us!
summary:
Sol by Sol: Outpost Commander is an interactive, browser-based space mission trainer developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to inspire the Artemis generation (ages 7–12). 

Addressing the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, we developed a zero-install simulation where players command lunar and Martian outposts. Players make real scientific trade-offs across three critical life-support pillars: Power, Air & Food (ECLSS), and Radiation Shielding. The game integrates authentic NASA DONKI space weather data, triggering real-time solar flare warnings where astronauts must analyze flare classifications and deploy deflector shields before radiation impacts the base.

Beyond resource strategy, players explore in full 3D: walking on cratered lunar and Martian regolith, driving exploration rovers, piloting star-cruisers, and stepping inside habitats and refineries.

This project is important because it demystifies complex space science—explaining terms like "sol," "radiation," and "space weather" in gentle, kid-friendly language—transforming real planetary data into an accessible, empowering STEM learning experience.
details:
What does it do?

Sol by Sol: Outpost Commander is an interactive, browser-based space mission trainer designed for junior astronauts (ages 7-12). Players take command of an outpost on both Mars and the Moon, balancing three core life-support resources: Power, Life Support (Oxygen & Food), and Radiation Shielding.

How does it work?

The game connects directly to the NASA DONKI (Database of Notifications, Knowledge, and Information) API. When real solar flare events (X-class or M-class) occur, the game triggers authentic space weather alerts. Players must calculate trade-offs, manage power grids, and raise deflector shields or take shelter before radiation impacts crew health. If offline, it gracefully uses verified NASA historical records.

Creative & Educational Impact:

- Explorable 3D WebGL Simulation: Players can walk on Martian and Lunar regolith, drive multi-wheel exploration rovers, pilot star-cruisers, and walk inside habitat pods, refineries, and hydroponic greenhouses.

- Plain Language for Kids: Complex terms like "Sol", "Solar Flare", "ECLSS", and "Radiation" are explained contextually in one clear, kid-friendly sentence.

- Gentle Failure & Replayability: Failing offers constructive feedback, teaching real scientific problem-solving.

Tools & Software Used:

- HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)

- Three.js WebGL 3D Engine

- Canvas 2D & Web Audio API

- NASA DONKI Open API
